01

A research-led path

I am a Computer Science and Engineering graduate of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET), and a Lecturer at Northern University Bangladesh. My research experience connects machine learning, optimization, and medical applications. I am preparing for doctoral research in Computer Science, with an interest in building medical AI systems whose objectives and evaluation reflect the structure of the problems they address.

Looking ahead / Doctoral direction

Building on my work in hierarchical classification and NLP bias, I hope to investigate how structured objectives, uncertainty-aware evaluation, and optimization can support more dependable medical AI. Reinforcement learning and intelligent control are further interests I would like to explore.

02

Questions that guide my work

Structure-aware medical AI

Learning from patient dialogue while respecting relationships between medical specializations and diseases.

How can training objectives preserve clinically meaningful consistency across prediction levels?

Bias & model evaluation

Understanding how bias arises and propagates through NLP training pipelines and decoding strategies.

How can evaluation reveal failure patterns that aggregate performance measures overlook?

Optimization & sequential learning

Connecting experience in time-series modeling and ensemble tuning with an interest in reinforcement learning and intelligent control.

How can optimization improve learning from temporal signals and inform future medical AI research?

03

Research & publications

Graduate Researcher · CUETJun 2024 – Jul 2025

Hierarchical medical dialogue classification

Classifying patient conversations across 16 diseases and four medical specializations while maintaining consistency between the two levels.

Designed a hierarchical pipeline and custom multi-objective loss functions to jointly optimize inter-level consistency and classification accuracy. Fine-tuned BanglaBERT and ClinicalBERT and examined model complexity–performance trade-offs.

A portion of this thesis work was accepted at ICCIT 2025, as reported in the CV.

Hierarchical learning / Transformer models / Loss function design
Research Associate · Learnify Research LabMay 2025 – Present

Bias propagation in NLP systems

Understanding bias types and how their effects propagate across the NLP model development process.

Investigating 18 distinct bias types and propagation mechanisms across training pipelines and decoding strategies.

Survey paper published in Elsevier’s Array journal, as reported in the CV.

NLP / Bias analysis / Training and decoding
Research Collaborator · CUETMar – Jun 2025

Electrical load forecasting

Forecasting electrical demand from historical Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) load data.

Developed LSTM, ARIMA, and hybrid forecasting models. Applied signal decomposition, feature engineering, hyperparameter optimization, and ensemble tuning to capture seasonal demand patterns.

Reported 1.09% MAPE in the CV. Evaluation protocol and dataset period are not specified consistently in the source.

Time-series analysis / LSTM / ARIMA / Ensemble optimization

04

Selected implementations

Diabetic retinopathy detection

Combined five CNN architecture families—VGG, ResNet, InceptionV3, DenseNet, and EfficientNet—for multi-class retinal grading. Examined model agreement and uncertainty to guide ensemble weighting, with a Flask interface for inference.

TensorFlow · OpenCV · Flask
Explore code ↗

Competitive programming duel bot

Built an adaptive challenge and skill-matching system using the Codeforces API and Elo-based rating updates. The project explores feedback-based opponent pairing; it is not presented as a trained reinforcement learning agent.

Python · Discord.py · Codeforces API
